chunks: Aban narrated from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about selling pasture when it is flowing water, such that a man directs his water to the land and thereby irrigates the grass, and he is the one who dug the canal and the water belongs to him, planting with it whatever he wishes.
So he عليه السلام said: If the water belongs to him, then let him plant with it whatever he wishes and sell it for whatever he likes.

key_terms.النَّهَرَ: the canal or watercourse dug for irrigation
key_terms.الْكَلَإِ: pasture or herbage offered for grazing or use
key_terms.الْمَاءُ: the water that is the basis of ownership and cultivation rights
key_terms.بَيْعِ: sale or transaction involving ownership transfer
key_terms.سَيْحًا: flowing or conducted water used for irrigation
key_terms.مَائِهِ: his water, indicating proprietary water rights
key_terms.يَبِيعُهُ: he sells it, meaning the cultivated output or pasture
key_terms.يَزْرَعُ: he cultivates or plants with the water

ai.seo_question: Can a person sell pasture or crops grown using water from a canal he himself owns?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the sale of pasture or produce sustained by water that a person owns and channels to his land. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that if the water belongs to the person, he may cultivate with it as he wishes and sell the resulting produce for whatever price he chooses.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3861 - Aban narrated from Isma'il bin Al-Fadl who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (as) about selling pasture when it is irrigated by flowing water, where a man directs his water to the land, irrigates the grass, and he is the one who dug the canal and owns the water, planting with it whatever he wishes.
Imam (as) said: "If the water is his, then he may plant with it whatever he wishes and sell it for whatever he likes."
